title: I made a little multiplayer experience inspired by one of my favorite short stories, A Short Stay in Hell - Free to play
author: _Sarandi_
selftext:
Playable Link: [https://libraryofbabel.dev/](https://libraryofbabel.dev/)

I made a little experience based on one of my favorite books, [A Short Stay in Hell by Steven L. Peck.](https://shortstayinhell.com/) It's a story that has stayed with me for a long time, and I highly recommend reading it!

Like in the story, the experience places you in a hell inspired by Borges' Library of Babel. A library so vast that it contains every book ever written, or that could ever be written... think infinite monkeys with typewritters. 

>"On every floor were rows upon rows of books. Millions of them (you will see soon what a terrible underestimate this is)."

The goal is simple: **find something meaningful.** A word, a phrase, Shakespeare, the story of your life — anything worth preserving. When you find something, you can add it to a communal shelf for other players to discover and read.

I don't want to spoil too much, but suffice it to say, even finding a three-letter word will be incredibly difficult. Good luck!

The experience is multiplayer, and the world is persistent. Everyone spawns relatively close to one another, but you're free to wander off and explore the library on your own.

Maybe you'll find something. Maybe someone else already has.

And if you've read the book, you probably have a pretty good idea of what you're getting yourself into.

comments.author: Fusionism
comments.body: This is super cool, one of my most favorite books and I had an idea about creating something like this as well. So far just three letter words have been found, I found hug.

replies.author: _Sarandi_
replies.body:
yeah finding anything greater than 3 is proving difficult! if forget how many years the book descrives before they find their first word 😅 Every bookcase, shelf and book is unique and has an address, so thechnically we could stumble upon something - might just take some time. 

As far as location, it remebers where you are, though there is no way to return to spawn. I wrestled with the jump mechanic, and ultimatley could not come up with a good solution - but ill keep thinking through it. 

>!currently if you walk far enough, you might catch a glimpse of someone falling. or someone being chased by cult members. you could also find the tools used by these cultists and chase other players around. or you might end up getting chased yourself - the further from spawn the greater the risk. !<
